io.github.stacklok.overview:
## MarketNow — trust layer for AI agents

Two surfaces, one data plane:

- **Remote (streamable HTTP)** — `https://marketnow.site/api/mcp`: catalog and commerce tools (`search_skills`, `get_skill`, `get_categories`, `health`, `register_agent`, `recommend_skill`, `get_rep`, `get_bounties`) over a 71,000+ index of MCP servers/skills with Sentinel static-analysis scores, install-risk flags and scam-domain checks.
- **stdio** — `npx -y marketnow-mcp` (v1.16.0): the verification toolset: `verify_trust` (takes a `card_id` or an `atc_credential` object/string — not a server name), `check_revocation`, `fingerprint_tool`, `verify_atc_spec`.

**What a positive verdict establishes (cryptographic, fail-closed):** (1) the Ed25519 signature verifies over the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of the credential minus its signature field; (2) the signing key is the pinned trust anchor for the declared issuer — key selection is its own pipeline stage, so self-signed or wrong-key credentials fail there; (3) temporal validity; (4) status against the signed revocation registry. Each stage returns its own pass/fail evidence; any failure names the failing stage.

**Cryptographic vs heuristic.** The four stages above are deterministic cryptography. Sentinel scores (0–10; L1 static analysis, L2 sandbox) and domain-risk checks are heuristics, reported as separate clearly-labeled fields — they never feed the cryptographic verdict.

**Trusted issuers and keys.** Keys are pinned per issuer in the published trust-anchor set (`vectors/_test-ca-keys.json` in the conformance corpus); selection is per-stage auditable.

**Outside the assessment.** Runtime behavior of a verified server, prompt-injection resistance, and semantic truthfulness of tool descriptions are out of scope; `fingerprint_tool` (JCS + SHA-256 per tool definition) detects post-hoc tampering with definitions.

**Reproducible examples.** The conformance corpus publishes canonical bytes (hex/base64/text) with SHA-256/512 and expected per-stage outcomes for positives and negatives: `valid-atc` (verify=true), `invalid-signature`, `self-signed-atc` (untrusted issuer), `expired-atc`, `premature-atc`, `revoked-atc` (all verify=false) — github.com/alicelabs-llc/universal-trust-adapter (index v1.7.0, RFC 8785 JCS). Public checker: https://marketnow.site/uta/conformance
